lead_headline: Aurora industrial property hits $4.9M foreclosure—largest filing since May as subscribers notch net +4 yesterday

restaurant.blurb: Eleventh consecutive day without new leads—Saturday marks 264 hours since last detection as June freeze solidifies into nearly two full weeks. Active pipeline remains locked at 196 leads (108 openings, 88 closures).

foreclosure.blurb: Airport Road and Hughes Road industrial site in Aurora filed $4.9M foreclosure—Arapahoe County property scheduled for June 5 auction remains week's only $4M+ filing.

liquor.blurb: Day 36: June freeze reaches first Saturday—Colorado's licensing shutdown extends 36th consecutive day with zero applications filed, zero status changes across 12,396 tracked licenses. The May paralysis now controls June's opening six calendar days as state apparatus maintains complete radio silence. The invisible backlog grows while machinery posts longest documented freeze in modern Colorado regulatory history. Saturday marks first weekend day of month with zero movement as licensing shutdown extends into second full weekend.

reputation.blurb: Six mentions yesterday hold Friday momentum—BusinessDen logged 41 pickups across 10 sources in past 7 days, down 2% from prior week's 42 mentions, effectively flat. Denver Post led with 10 citations, Facebook contributed 9, Instagram 6. Notable Saturday coverage: Tenth Circuit rental car fee case (Kim Monson Show), Denver Housing CEO dismissal (Hoodline), Dick's Sporting Goods 'House of Sport' Thornton opening (Denver Post). Week shows stable citation velocity as media attention maintains plateau through first June weekend. Google News RSS continues driving 100% of discovery.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +4 yesterday (6 new, 2 canceled)—Friday breaks ten-day flatline with strongest single-day gain since May 28's net +6. MTD net climbs to +8 (+1.6/day), 90-day net rises to +134. The past two weeks reveal whipsaw pattern: May 26-28 produced net +11, then May 29-June 4 delivered ten straight zeros, now June 5 posts net +4 to finally crack month-opening freeze. YTD pace of +1.3/day sits below Friday's MTD rate as June shows first acquisition pulse after brutal opening-week paralysis that fully erased late-May momentum.
